intro.title: Compound Component (Tabs)
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a tabbed interface using Vue's compound component pattern. You'll create a set of components—Tabs, TabList, and TabPanel—that work together to manage and display content in separate tabs. The core concept is using Vue's provide/inject API to share state and methods between parent and child components without prop drilling. You'll learn to structure components for reusability and maintain a clean separation of concerns. By the end, you'll have a functional tab system where clicking a tab button shows its corresponding content panel.
intro.usecase: Compound components like Tabs are essential in modern web applications where complex UI needs to be modular and reusable. You'll find them in dashboard interfaces where users switch between different data views, in e-commerce product pages that toggle between descriptions, reviews, and specifications, and in settings panels that organize options into categorized sections. As a Vue developer, you'll implement this pattern to create maintainable tabbed navigation for admin panels, user profiles, or multi-step forms where content needs logical grouping without tight coupling between components.
